newsitem.title: UK: Bank of England raises interest rate to 6.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bank of England raises interest rate to 6.5 percent.

text.p: The Bank of England's new monetary policy committee, which has been put in charge of interest rates by the Labour government, raised official rates to 6.5 percent from 6.25 percent after its first meeting on Friday.
It was the first time since the central bank was nationalised in 1945 that it had changed interest rates without being instructed by the government.

The Bank said recent economic data were consistent with the view it took in its Inflation Report last month that "on present evidence, there is still likely to be a need for some further moderate tightening of policy in the months ahead."
"The Committee accordingly voted to raise the Bank's repo rate by 0.25 percent to 6.50 percent," the bank said in a statement.

"It believes that this action to tighten the monetary stance, taken with the aim of meeting the government's inflation target, offers the best chance of achieving continued growth in output and employment at a sustainable pace."
